rituals.name: THREE CHANGES
rituals.goal: Find one thing already moving.
rituals.mission: Find one thing already moving.
rituals.rule: Guess whether you can follow it through three changes without losing the thought completely.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether you can follow it through three changes without losing the thought completely.
rituals.play: Pick a cursor, fan, shadow, leaf, person, reflection—anything moving. Track three changes: direction, speed, shape, position, brightness.
rituals.twist: Now try to recall the exact wording of the thought from before the third change.
rituals.mindBend: Your thought didn’t disappear. It just lost exclusive access to you.
rituals.mind_bend: Your thought didn’t disappear. It just lost exclusive access to you.
rituals.why: The thought may still exist, but it lost uninterrupted access to the attention channel.
rituals.reveal: The thought may still exist, but it lost uninterrupted access to the attention channel.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.name: PERIPHERAL DOOR
rituals.goal: Stress loves a tunnel.
rituals.mission: Stress loves a tunnel.
rituals.rule: Guess how many objects you can notice at the edges without moving your head.
rituals.one_rule: Guess how many objects you can notice at the edges without moving your head.
rituals.play: Keep your gaze softly on one point. Without turning, name the farthest thing you can detect on the left, right, above and below.
rituals.twist: Feel whether the scene becomes wider than the problem in the centre.
rituals.mindBend: A narrowed mind often arrives with a narrowed field of view.
rituals.mind_bend: A narrowed mind often arrives with a narrowed field of view.
rituals.why: Widening visual attention can compete with the narrow attentional style of threat.
rituals.reveal: Widening visual attention can compete with the narrow attentional style of threat.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.name: SOUND UNTIL IT CHANGES
rituals.goal: Choose one sound and wait for it to betray its own sameness.
rituals.mission: Choose one sound and wait for it to betray its own sameness.
rituals.rule: Guess how long it will stay exactly the same.
rituals.one_rule: Guess how long it will stay exactly the same.
rituals.play: Pick a continuous sound: aircon, traffic, hum, rain, fridge. Listen only for the first change in pitch, volume, rhythm or distance.
rituals.twist: Catch the moment “constant” becomes obviously variable.
rituals.mindBend: What feels continuous is often changing underneath your label for it.
rituals.mind_bend: What feels continuous is often changing underneath your label for it.
rituals.why: Attention reveals micro-changes that a stressed brain compresses into “this is just how it is.”
rituals.reveal: Attention reveals micro-changes that a stressed brain compresses into “this is just how it is.”
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the chosen example to one brief experiment. If it starts making you less steady, more confused or more stuck, stop and return to the concrete facts in front of you. The result is a working perspective, not proof that the opposite story is true.

rituals.preciseSubpattern: Assuming sensations stay constant

rituals.challenge: Assuming sensations stay constant
rituals.recognition_cue: Assuming sensations stay constant
rituals.theory_backbone: Sensory discrimination; impermanence; attentional training
rituals.mechanism_fingerprint: Monitor a seemingly continuous sound for its first detectable micro-variation to disconfirm perceptual constancy.

rituals.name: TEMPERATURE COIN
rituals.goal: Touch something cool or warm and make a prediction before your skin votes.
rituals.mission: Touch something cool or warm and make a prediction before your skin votes.
rituals.rule: Guess how many seconds the strongest sensation will last.
rituals.one_rule: Guess how many seconds the strongest sensation will last.
rituals.play: Touch a safe cool or warm object for one second. Remove it. Count slowly until the sensation changes category—strong to mild, sharp to vague, local to spread.
rituals.twist: Compare the predicted duration with the actual change point.
rituals.mindBend: A sensation can be intense without being stable.
rituals.mind_bend: A sensation can be intense without being stable.
rituals.why: Body sensations are dynamic, and prediction often overestimates how fixed they will feel.
rituals.reveal: Body sensations are dynamic, and prediction often overestimates how fixed they will feel.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use only comfortably mild temperatures and brief skin contact—no ice, very hot objects or prolonged exposure. Stop with pain, numbness, burning, or a lasting change in skin colour.

rituals.challenge: Expectations shaping sensation
rituals.recognition_cue: Expectations shaping sensation
rituals.theory_backbone: Interoception; prediction error; sensory habituation
rituals.mechanism_fingerprint: Predict post-contact thermal sensation duration and compare with actual qualitative transition timing.

rituals.name: JAW CONTRAST
rituals.goal: Make tension obvious on purpose so release has something to compare with.
rituals.mission: Make tension obvious on purpose so release has something to compare with.
rituals.rule: Guess whether your jaw is already closer to “soft” or “clenched.”
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether your jaw is already closer to “soft” or “clenched.”
rituals.play: Gently clench your jaw for three seconds—no pain—then let it hang loose. Do nothing else.
rituals.twist: Notice which state suddenly becomes easier to identify because you created contrast.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes calm is easier to find after you show the body what “not calm” feels like.
rituals.mind_bend: Sometimes calm is easier to find after you show the body what “not calm” feels like.
rituals.why: The nervous system notices differences better than vague instructions to “relax.”
rituals.reveal: The nervous system notices differences better than vague instructions to “relax.”
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use only a gentle, short jaw contraction—no hard clenching. Stop for tooth pain, jaw pain, locking, painful clicking or facial discomfort.

rituals.recognition_cue: Unnoticed voluntary amplification of arousal
rituals.theory_backbone: Progressive muscle relaxation; sensory contrast; interoception
rituals.mechanism_fingerprint: Brief safe voluntary jaw contraction creates a contrast reference for detecting release state.

rituals.name: THREE SLOW BLINK CUTS
rituals.goal: Your eyes have a built-in edit button.
rituals.mission: Your eyes have a built-in edit button.
rituals.rule: Guess whether three slow blinks will make the scene feel continuous or slightly reset.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether three slow blinks will make the scene feel continuous or slightly reset.
rituals.play: Blink slowly three times. Each time, notice the instant the visual world disappears and returns.
rituals.twist: Catch the tiny “new frame” feeling after each reopening.
rituals.mindBend: The scene feels continuous because your brain edits the cuts out.
rituals.mind_bend: The scene feels continuous because your brain edits the cuts out.
rituals.why: Perception is stitched from interruptions, even when experience feels continuous.
rituals.reveal: Perception is stitched from interruptions, even when experience feels continuous.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Blink gently at your natural pace. Do not squeeze the eyes shut, prolong the blinks or repeat them to chase the visual cut; stop for eye pain, marked dryness, dizziness or unusual visual symptoms.

rituals.theory_backbone: Perceptual continuity; attentional reset; visual interruption
rituals.mechanism_fingerprint: Exploit normal blink-induced visual interruption to make perceptual continuity consciously noticeable.

rituals.name: FOUR CORNERS
rituals.goal: Keep the thought.
rituals.mission: Keep the thought.
rituals.rule: Guess whether the thought can stay present while your eyes visit four corners of the room.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether the thought can stay present while your eyes visit four corners of the room.
rituals.play: Without moving your head much, look to four corners in a slow square. At each corner, name one shape or line.
rituals.twist: Notice the thought and visual task can coexist without either taking over.
rituals.mindBend: A thought can be in the room without becoming the room.
rituals.mind_bend: A thought can be in the room without becoming the room.
rituals.why: Attention can contain a thought without being identical to the thought.
rituals.reveal: Attention can contain a thought without being identical to the thought.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.name: COLOUR POP-OUT
rituals.goal: Pick a colour.
rituals.mission: Pick a colour.
rituals.rule: Guess how many objects of that colour you will notice in ten seconds.
rituals.one_rule: Guess how many objects of that colour you will notice in ten seconds.
rituals.play: Choose a colour you were not thinking about. Scan the room for 10 sec and count every appearance.
rituals.twist: Ask whether those objects appeared—or whether your attention changed.
rituals.mindBend: What you notice more is not always what exists more.
rituals.mind_bend: What you notice more is not always what exists more.
rituals.why: Once the brain sets a search target, matching information suddenly feels more frequent.
rituals.reveal: Once the brain sets a search target, matching information suddenly feels more frequent.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.name: PULSE WITHOUT A STORY
rituals.goal: Find a body signal and ban the biography for ten seconds.
rituals.mission: Find a body signal and ban the biography for ten seconds.
rituals.rule: Guess whether you can describe the sensation without using an emotion word.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether you can describe the sensation without using an emotion word.
rituals.play: Notice your pulse, chest, throat or stomach. Describe only physical properties: fast, slow, tight, warm, fluttery, heavy, moving. No “anxious,” “bad,” “dangerous,” or “because.”

rituals.mission: Keep the sentence.

rituals.mindBend: A thought’s volume is not proof of its importance.
rituals.mind_bend: A thought’s volume is not proof of its importance.

rituals.name: WORD MELT
rituals.goal: Pick the one word with too much power and make it sound like noise.
rituals.mission: Pick the one word with too much power and make it sound like noise.
rituals.rule: Guess how many repetitions it takes before the word starts sounding strange.

rituals.play: Choose one safe loaded word from the thought—failure, awkward, rejected, ruined. Repeat it steadily 20 times, listening to the sound rather than the meaning.

rituals.name: ONE-JOINT WEATHER
rituals.goal: Change exactly one joint and see if the emotional weather notices.
rituals.mission: Change exactly one joint and see if the emotional weather notices.
rituals.rule: Guess whether moving only your shoulders, hands or jaw will change anything at all.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether moving only your shoulders, hands or jaw will change anything at all.
rituals.play: Freeze your current posture. Rate its tension from 0–10. Change one joint only—drop shoulders, uncurl hands, uncross ankles. Re-rate.
rituals.twist: Look for even a one-point change without trying to “feel better.”
rituals.mindBend: You do not have to change your whole mood to change one ingredient.
rituals.mind_bend: You do not have to change your whole mood to change one ingredient.
rituals.why: Body configuration is one ingredient in state, not merely a passive result of it.
rituals.reveal: Body configuration is one ingredient in state, not merely a passive result of it.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Change only one joint or posture point within an easy, pain-free range. Do not force a stretch or hold tension; return to neutral if you get pain, numbness, dizziness or instability.

rituals.name: HALF-SPEED HANDS
rituals.goal: Do one ordinary movement at half speed and see whether the deadline explodes.
rituals.mission: Do one ordinary movement at half speed and see whether the deadline explodes.
rituals.rule: Guess what will happen if your hands move slowly for fifteen seconds.
rituals.one_rule: Guess what will happen if your hands move slowly for fifteen seconds.
rituals.play: Pick a harmless action—put down a cup, type one short sentence, fold a tissue—and do it at deliberately half your normal speed.
rituals.twist: Check if urgency rises, falls, or simply complains while time keeps moving normally.
rituals.mindBend: Urgency is a sensation. A deadline is a fact. They sometimes travel separately.
rituals.mind_bend: Urgency is a sensation. A deadline is a fact. They sometimes travel separately.
rituals.why: The feeling of rush can persist even when slower behaviour causes no consequence.
rituals.reveal: The feeling of rush can persist even when slower behaviour causes no consequence.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.name: EYES-CLOSED MAP
rituals.goal: Your brain thinks it knows the room.
rituals.mission: Your brain thinks it knows the room.
rituals.rule: Guess how accurately you can point to three objects with your eyes closed.
rituals.one_rule: Guess how accurately you can point to three objects with your eyes closed.
rituals.play: Look around once. Close your eyes. Point to three objects one by one. Open your eyes and compare the angles.
rituals.twist: Notice even small errors between the internal map and the actual room.
rituals.mindBend: A vivid internal model can still be an approximation.
rituals.mind_bend: A vivid internal model can still be an approximation.
rituals.why: The brain confidently fills missing spatial detail all day long.
rituals.reveal: The brain confidently fills missing spatial detail all day long.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stay still in a clear space and point without reaching toward furniture or objects. Open your eyes before taking a step, and stop if you feel unsteady or disoriented.

rituals.name: NEXT BREATH ARRIVES
rituals.goal: For once, do not improve your breathing.
rituals.mission: For once, do not improve your breathing.
rituals.rule: Guess whether breathing will become unsafe, chaotic, or simply continue if you stop managing it for three breaths.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether breathing will become unsafe, chaotic, or simply continue if you stop managing it for three breaths.
rituals.play: For three breaths, make no effort to deepen, slow, count or perfect anything. Just notice the instant each next breath begins on its own.
rituals.twist: Catch the body initiating what you were tempted to supervise.
rituals.mindBend: You do not have to personally manage every breath for breathing to happen.
rituals.mind_bend: You do not have to personally manage every breath for breathing to happen.
rituals.why: Some regulation happens better when you stop turning it into a performance review.
rituals.reveal: Some regulation happens better when you stop turning it into a performance review.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the breath unforced and ordinary. If you catch yourself holding, over-breathing or trying to produce a result, stop; end the exercise if you feel faint or more short of breath.

rituals.name: FOREGROUND / BACKGROUND SWAP
rituals.goal: Let’s move one sound out of the starring role without making it stop.
rituals.mission: Let’s move one sound out of the starring role without making it stop.
rituals.rule: Pick the loudest sound. Guess whether it still feels dominant after you deliberately promote a quieter sound.
rituals.one_rule: Pick the loudest sound. Guess whether it still feels dominant after you deliberately promote a quieter sound.
rituals.play: Listen to the loudest sound for five seconds. Find the faintest sound you can detect and give only that sound five seconds of attention.
rituals.twist: Check if the loud sound changed—or whether your attention changed its rank.
rituals.mindBend: You do not always need silence; sometimes you need a different foreground.
rituals.mind_bend: You do not always need silence; sometimes you need a different foreground.
rituals.why: Sensory dominance is partly about volume and partly about where attention points.
rituals.reveal: Sensory dominance is partly about volume and partly about where attention points.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the listening pass to one brief experiment. If it starts making you less steady, more confused or more stuck, stop and return to the concrete facts in front of you. Stop at the planned endpoint rather than repeating the ritual until it feels completely convincing.

rituals.name: COMPLEMENTARY COLOUR ECHO
rituals.goal: Your eyes can keep a colour after the object is gone.
rituals.mission: Your eyes can keep a colour after the object is gone.
rituals.rule: Guess what colour ghost appears after staring at one safe coloured object.
rituals.one_rule: Guess what colour ghost appears after staring at one safe coloured object.
rituals.play: Look at a non-bright coloured object for about fifteen seconds, then shift to a plain white or light wall. Don’t use lights or the sun.
rituals.twist: Catch the faint complementary colour that may appear.
rituals.mindBend: Seeing something after it is gone can be a property of the visual system, not of the world.
rituals.mind_bend: Seeing something after it is gone can be a property of the visual system, not of the world.
rituals.why: Visual receptors adapt, and the contrast system keeps processing after the stimulus leaves.
rituals.reveal: Visual receptors adapt, and the contrast system keeps processing after the stimulus leaves.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use an ordinary non-glare object and a comfortable gaze; never use the sun, bright lamps, lasers or anything painful to look at. Stop for eye pain, headache, dizziness or a visual effect that lingers unexpectedly.

rituals.ritualText:
PLAY TIME
60 sec

GAME
SOUND FOLLOWS THE FACE

GOAL
Your brain likes sound to come from where the action looks like it is happening.

ONE RULE
Guess whether a voice feels located closer to a moving face than to the actual speaker.

PLAY
Play a safe audio source while looking at a visible object or screen that appears to 'speak.' Notice where the sound seems to belong.

TWIST
Catch the location shift created by visual capture.

MIND BEND
Where a sound seems to come from is partly negotiated between senses.

SAFETY
PAUSE
Do this pass once and keep the result provisional. If the exercise increases distress or confusion, stop rather than trying harder. The result is a working perspective, not proof that the opposite story is true.
